title: The Óbidos Double
title_candidates: The Week the Course Book Was Rewritten
Eighteen Points Clear, Thirteen Shots Clear
theme: On four days of the Lisbon Coast the record book was rewritten in both directions at once — Jon Baker rebuilt himself into a double winner (Trophy and Jacket, by 18 and 13) with a new Royal Óbidos course record, while at the other end of the same fairways Alex Baker and John Patterson posted course-worsts and Gregg Williams quietly sank from third to the Spoon. The Lisbon Coast gave and it took, often on the same hole.
tone: house — faithful, tongue-in-cheek, Ronay/Peck register: witty, characterful, anchored in the numbers, gently ribbing insiders who were there
opening_hook: Open on R3 at Royal Óbidos: Jon Baker double-bogeys the 1st and hands the Jacket lead away after 35 holes in front (b01), Mullin nudges ahead by the 6th (b07) — and then Baker answers with 20 points in six holes (b05) and an 86 that is the lowest gross the course has ever seen (cr02). That afternoon is where both trophies were settled; Act One backs up to explain how the field got there.
foreshadow: Jon Baker arrives with three prior Trophies and three prior Jackets but finishes of 4th, 4th and 4th on the Trophy in TEGs 14–16 — the win has been overdue
Gregg Williams arrives as the form man: TEG 15 Trophy winner, back-to-back Jacket wins, and only one Spoon in his life
Alex Baker is the reigning Spoon holder with back-to-back Spoons — and gets off to precisely the start you would expect at Praia D'El Rey's 5th
Four rounds, four course records — two brilliant, two catastrophic; the Lisbon Coast keeps rewriting its own extremes

competitions.name: Trophy (Stableford)
competitions.how: Baker opened 38 and sat a point behind Patterson after R1; he took the lead on the 1st hole of R2 at West Cliffs (b46) and never gave it back, back-to-back 44s at West Cliffs and Royal Óbidos turning a 2-point lead into 11, and a solid 40 in R4 stretching it to 18. 166 points, 9th best in TEG history and his own personal best.

competitions.name: Green Jacket (Gross)
competitions.how: Baker led the gross from R1 H2 but lost it after 35 holes in front when he double-bogeyed the R3 1st (b01); Mullin was outright ahead by the 6th (b07). Baker retook it at the 7th and never looked back, signing for an 86 that broke the Royal Óbidos course record (cr02) and closing at +67, 13 clear of Mullin — despite two 9s in R4 (b21, b22).

competitions.name: Wooden Spoon
competitions.how: Williams was third after R1 with a 33 and a 93 that was seven better than his last Praia D'El Rey visit; he slipped to fourth in R2, then a seven-hole procession of doubles from the 12th at Royal Óbidos (b49) dropped him to the bottom at H14 (b25) and a round of 26. A 29 in R4, opened with a 9 at the 1st (b20), sealed it on 123 points — the first Spoon for the man who won TEG 15.

headline_candidates: Praia D'El Rey Sets a New Low Bar
Patterson Leads, Alex Baker Makes History the Wrong Way
rounds.angle: Patterson edges the opening day by a point and Mullin's back nine sings, but the round's record belongs to Alex Baker, whose 114 is the worst gross ever posted at Praia D'El Rey.

headline_candidates: West Cliffs, Both Ends of the Book
Thirty-Four Shots Apart on the Same Links
rounds.angle: On one links, in one round, the West Cliffs course record falls and the course-worst is set — while Jon Baker takes the Trophy lead on the very first hole and never surrenders it.

headline_candidates: Lost at the 1st, Won by the 16th
rounds.chosen_headline: Lost at the 1st, Won by the 16th
rounds.angle: Baker loses a 35-hole Jacket lead at the R3 1st and Mullin goes outright ahead by the 6th — then Baker piles up 20 points in six holes and signs the lowest gross Royal Óbidos has ever given up.

headline_candidates: Baker Wins Both While Losing Shots
Nine, Nine, and Still Eighteen Clear
rounds.chosen_headline: Nine, Nine, and Still Eighteen Clear
rounds.angle: Baker can afford two 9s and still win by 18 and 13; behind him Alex Baker bleeds 25 shots in nine holes and Patterson's 9 and 10 close out a chastening finish.

players.arc: Three straight 4th places on the Trophy answered in emphatic style: a personal-best 166, the Jacket at +67, a new Royal Óbidos course record and a 15-shot improvement on his last West Cliffs visit — the double, and no arguments.

Nine prior Jackets and the only man to properly test Baker: a 12-shot personal best and a new course record at West Cliffs, outright gross leader for one hole at Royal Óbidos, and runner-up in both competitions.
The reigning Jacket holder and TEG 15 Trophy winner slid from third after R1 to the Spoon, undone by a seven-hole run of doubles at Royal Óbidos and a 9 to open R4.

Led the Trophy after R1 and set a personal best at Royal Óbidos, but his week is remembered for West Cliffs: a worst-ever +44, 27 shots gone in eight holes, and the highest gross the course has ever seen.

Back-to-back Spoon holder who avoided a third only because Williams collapsed faster — new Praia D'El Rey course-worst in R1, four separate blow-ups of 8 or more at Royal Óbidos, 25 shots gone in nine holes in R4, and one genuine bright spot: a personal best at West Cliffs.

cuts: b07 is retained but the remaining routine lead-change beats are cut: b46 kept for the Trophy takeover, b48 used only as a summary
venue_notes: TEG's 6th trip to the Lisbon Coast and, at Praia D'El Rey, the 5th and 6th TEG rounds at the venue — familiar enough that a new course-worst there (cr01, across 24 prior visits) genuinely stings. West Cliffs is only the 2nd TEG round at Cynthia Dye's 2017 links, and it produced both extremes in a single day (cr03, cr04). Royal Óbidos — Seve's last design, 4th TEG round there — is the pivot: water, drama, and a new course record. Use the coastal-dunes back nine at Praia D'El Rey to frame R4's carnage (Alex Baker's 5th-to-13th collapse, Patterson's 14th and 15th).
course_history_notes: Alex Baker's 114 in R1 is the worst gross in 24 prior TEG visits to Praia D'El Rey — and he was 11 shots worse than his last visit there (cr01).
Jon Baker's R3 86 broke the Royal Óbidos record set across 18 prior visits, was his own new PB there (previous best 89, TEG 9) and 8 shots better than his last visit (cr02).
David Mullin's R2 82 lowered the West Cliffs record from 88 and was 12 shots better than his own last visit; Jon Baker improved on his 2015 West Cliffs mark by 15 (cr03).
John Patterson's West Cliffs 116 was 19 shots worse than his TEG 15 visit and the highest gross the course has recorded (cr04) — yet he set a personal best of 94 at Royal Óbidos two days later.
decisive_moments: Trophy: R2 H1 at West Cliffs — Jon Baker takes the outright lead from Patterson (b46) and holds it for the remaining 71 holes, back-to-back 44s making the 18-point final margin inevitable.
Green Jacket: R3 H7 at Royal Óbidos — Baker retakes the gross lead within a hole of losing it (b01, b07) and turns it into the course record 86 (cr02), an 8-shot cushion he extends to 13.
Wooden Spoon: R3 H14 at Royal Óbidos — Gregg Williams's double bogey mid-way through a seven-hole run of doubles drops him to last (b25, b49) on a round of 26, and he never climbs out.
Green Jacket: R3 H7 at Royal Óbidos

payoffs.seed: Jon Baker's three straight 4th-place Trophy finishes
payoffs.resolves_in: Round 4 / How the three were decided
payoffs.payoff: 166 points, a personal best and 9th best in TEG history, plus the Jacket at +67 — a double from a man who had finished 4th on the Trophy three TEGs running (b02, b03).

payoffs.seed: Gregg Williams as the form man (TEG 15 Trophy, back-to-back Jackets, one career Spoon)
payoffs.resolves_in: Round 3 and the Wooden Spoon section
payoffs.payoff: Seven consecutive doubles from the Royal Óbidos 12th (b49) drops him to last at H14 (b25); a 9 at the R4 1st (b20) confirms 123 points and his second career Spoon (b15).

payoffs.seed: Alex Baker, reigning and back-to-back Spoon holder
payoffs.payoff: A 10 at the Praia D'El Rey 5th (SI 2) and a 9 at the 18th add up to 114, the course's worst-ever gross (cr01, b08, b18) — but he escapes a third straight Spoon because Williams fell further, despite bleeding 25 shots in nine holes in R4 (b04).

payoffs.seed: Four rounds, records in both directions
payoffs.payoff: West Cliffs surrenders its record and its worst on the same day (cr03, cr04), Royal Óbidos its record to Jon Baker (cr02) — four course records in four rounds, two glorious, two grim.
